rewardkit 0.1.7 source copy (cw-strict-worktree/.../rewardkit-0.1.7-source: models.py, reward.py, judges.py, runner.py) for aggregation/likert/timeout/order semantics
evidence: STATIC/STRUCTURAL REVIEW (no ranking run). (1) Reward formula: frozen tests/tools/score.py (byte-identical to rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/tools/score.py; test.sh also identical to template) computes reward = weighted mean of functional/polish/visual with weights 0.6/0.2/0.2 (tests/scoring.toml [weights], identical to template), zeroed only when a zero-weight gate (render, constraints) is not >0 or functional <= floor 0.05. Each term is non-decreasing in its dimension score and gates/floor are upper-sets, so reward is componentwise monotone: an app that is at least as good in every dimension can never score lower. Function (0.6) outweighs craft (0.4); the floor stops a functionally dead app farming polish/visual. (2) Within dimensions: rewardkit 0.1.7 (pinned tests/Dockerfile:31) weighted_mean (reward.py _weighted_mean) is monotone in criterion passes; likert normalize=(raw-1)/(points-1) clamped (models.py:47), so visual anchors 0 and 1 tie at 0.0 - a tie, not an inversion. Functional criterion weights (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml lines 41-254, total 33.0) put the core promises highest (deleted_and_expired 4.0, signin_and_client_scope 3.0, sent_once/search_transcript 2.5, walls/timers/holds/persistence 2.0, the rest 1.5); no craft criterion outweighs a core behaviour. (3) Gates a stronger app could fail: render (gates/render/judge.toml:25-34) checks only sign-in, wrong-password refusal and nothing private before sign-in (instruction.md:7, walls-and-retention.md:45); constraints (gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-37) has Gwen post in M-11 (her matter, 7-day timer, posted at the fixed clock so it cannot expire) and Harriet (partner, not walled per seed) read it in a separate context. Both are public requirements a conforming app satisfies; neither depends on a golden-only default. (4) Mutation-order inversions checked (rewardkit runs suites sorted functional->polish->visual with --max-concurrent-agent 1; individual mode runs criteria sequentially in listed order, judges.py:467-494): timer_changes shortening M-13 to 7 days deletes only K-13 (4 May) in a correct app; K-8 'Draft will sent for your review.' (10 May) survives, so later message_links and live_updates_keep_my_work do not penalise a correct timer implementation relative to a broken one. hold release deletes only K-17; persistence step c is state-relative; Sian/Dev walls are lifted at criterion end and polish/visual use only Gwen; polish hold_mark relies on K-7 which no criterion releases. A per-criterion judge timeout scores only that criterion 0 (judges.py timeout path -> _timeout_scores), so a slow-to-verify strong app ties, not trails, a fast-failing weak one on that criterion. (5) Tried broken-but-passing and conforming-but-failing apps: a static/seed facade fails the constraints gate (cross-context readback); a polished app with near-dead function is capped by the 0.05 floor and by polish/visual needing real timer label/hold mark/transcript; a conforming app with long pasted message links must still meet the public 390 px no-sideways-scroll requirement (integration-independent, conversations.md:33), not a hidden demand. Minor non-blocking edge: the single 2.0 persistence criterion grades durability of whatever exists (functional judge.toml:251-266, 'a feature that did not work before the restart is graded in its own criterion'), so an app with edits that work in-session but revert on restart (edits +1.5, persistence -2.0) can trail an app with no edit feature at all by 0.5/33 x 0.6 = 0.009 reward; that app breaks the public 'restarts keep ... edits and their versions' rule (integration.md:38), so I do not count it as a credible inversion of a better app. (6) Required measurement MISSING: qc/runs/kittle-2026-10-09-r4/raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'; its six indexed artifacts re-hash to the listed SHA256 and contain only scripted golden PASS observations (golden-run.log: 16 functional + gate_constraints + polish_refusal_in_place PASS), with no mutated weak app or ordered reward run. The workbook Internal Quality Checks row 42 note reads 'Mukesh - we need to monitor this one', and qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md requires a hash-bound runtime reward-ordering record before clearance. Design is monotone on inspection, but ranking is unmeasured, so risk stays true.
